title: Separate space from inode capacity
goal: Diagnose supplied space and inode shortages without causing either one.
challenge: Compare live byte/inode availability and classify both synthetic cases. Explain what each counter can establish and propose a safe next investigation, without filling a filesystem or deleting unrelated files.

steps.explanation: Create a unique private guest workspace. Retain its printed path; repeat starts a new workspace, never overwrites old evidence. Stop if creation/change-directory fails.
steps.expected: A new /home/learner/capacity-space.XXXXXX directory. All files below are guest-local.

steps.explanation: Compare current byte capacity, inode capacity and this small workspace.
steps.expected: Units differ; du does not enumerate every cause of df/du differences.

steps.command: printf '%s\n' 'SYNTHETIC cases; not this VM' 'case available_KiB free_inodes' 'A 1024 500000' 'B 1048576 0' > shortages.txt
steps.explanation: Type the exact tiny dataset; both cases are hypothetical.
steps.expected: A has only 1 MiB available despite many inodes. B has 1 GiB available and no free inodes.

steps.explanation: Interpret capacity for new file creation.
steps.expected: Either resource can prevent creation. Diagnose inode usage without assuming file contents are large.

steps.explanation: Verify the exercise created only a tiny dataset.
steps.expected: No exhaustion workload ran; current VM may show neither fault.

hints: Compare df -Pk with df -Pi: one reports blocks, the other inodes.
A filesystem can have room for bytes but no available inode for a new file.
Do not fill the VM to recreate a fictional example.
review: I classified A as byte-space shortage and B as inode shortage.
I separated the examples from live evidence and proposed scoped investigation.
coverage: Partial 200.1 capacity symptoms; preparation for filesystem administration, not repair. Completion records self-review, not verified guest assessment; there is no score.
